subject: Acme Health — private endpoint egress rules and allowlist guidance
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaSInfra Team <saasinfra@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 20:03:00 -0500
Subject: Private deployment: allowlist, firewall and egress needs (Acme Health)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We're moving forward with the private deployment evaluation and need a concise list of networking controls for our infra/security teams to implement. Specifically we need:

- IP ranges or FQDNs to allow for Redwood private endpoints (control and data).
- Required outbound ports/protocols and recommended firewall policies (stateful rules, timeout expectations).
- Guidance on telemetrics/health-check endpoints and whether those require explicit egress.
- Any recommended patterns for using an outbound proxy or NAT gateway with tokenized traffic.

I've attached a snapshot of our current edge firewall policy and a simplified network diagram. Our security team prefers allowlist by IP where possible, but we can support FQDN-based egress for telemetry if that's the only option.

Can you send something we can present to our firewall and SOC teams today? We're targeting a pilot this month.

Appreciate it,
Jared
Director, Cloud Engineering
Acme Health
Attachments: acme_firewall_snapshot.pdf (PDF), network-diagram-vpc.png (PNG)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: allowlist, firewall and egress needs (Acme Health)

Jared — thanks for the details and the attachments. Drafting the short checklist below for your SOC & networking teams; I've attached a CSV allowlist template they can drop into their change request. CC'ing Dev (infra/runtime) and Hannah (security) for any technical addenda.

Summary (pilot-ready):
- Inbound (to Redwood-managed private endpoint):
  - Allow connections from your application subnets to the Private Endpoint IPs we will provide. For the pilot we'll give fixed /32 IPs per endpoint; in production you can request CIDR prefixes.
  - Protocol: TCP port 443 only. TLS required; mutual TLS not required for hosted private endpoints (certificate pinning handled at the endpoint).
- Outbound (egress) required from your environment to Redwood services:
  - Telemetry & metrics: telemetry.redwood.com (currently resolves to ephemeral IPs) — prefer FQDN allowlist if dynamic, otherwise allow the following ranges: 34.210.120.0/22, 18.197.64.0/22 (note: these are service egress clusters and may expand).
  - Model updates & metadata: updates.redwood.com (443).
  - Health checks & reporting: status.redwood.com (443).
  - If you enforce IP-only allowlisting, request the official ranges from your Redwood engagement lead; we'll provide an up-to-date CIDR list before pilot cutover and on every release.
- Ports / protocols:
  - Outbound TCP 443 (HTTPS) to the above FQDNs is required.
  - Outbound to cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., STS endpoints) is not used by Redwood in the private endpoint flow; block as you normally do.
- Egress considerations:
  - Preferred: allow FQDNs for telemetry to avoid brittle CIDR rules. If FQDN not supported, use the CIDR list we provide and plan for monthly updates.
  - If outbound egress is restricted, you can route telemetry through an internal HTTP proxy; Redwood supports traffic via a forward proxy that does TLS passthrough (proxy must support CONNECT to target host:443).
  - For air-gapped/on-prem: we support an on-prem runtime bundle — see note below (additional licensing & sync windows).
- Firewall policy & session timeouts:
  - Keep-alive: connections to private endpoints expect persistent TLS sessions. Idle TCP timeout should be >= 120s.
  - Stateful inspection OK; avoid aggressive half-closed pruning.

Attached: redwood_private_allowlist_template.csv (columns: hostname, ip_cidr, description, required_by_date).

Action items for Acme SOC:
- Confirm whether you can allow the above FQDNs; if not, reply and we'll produce a CIDR snapshot.
- If using an outbound proxy, share proxy hostname and we will test from our end.
- If you need mTLS enforced on the wire, we can scope that into the private deployment plan (extra config & cert exchange).

Dev/Hannah — any additional infra/security caveats to add?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_private_allowlist_template.csv (CSV)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: allowlist, firewall and egress needs (Acme Health)

Adding a few technical specifics for the pilot that the network ops team will want:

- Exact ports: inbound 443 (TLS) to endpoint IPs. Outbound 443 to telemetry/update FQDNs. No other ports required for normal inference traffic.
- IP consolidation: if you must allow by CIDR, aggregate ranges to /22 where possible to reduce ruleset churn. We'll supply the minimal set.
- NAT/GW behavior: connections originating in your VPC/subnets should NAT to your egress IPs. Whitelist those egress IPs if your firewall sits upstream. If you run multiple AZs, ensure each AZ's NAT has a consistent egress IP for easier rules.
- TLS inspection: we strongly recommend NOT performing TLS termination that rewrites client-server certs for our private endpoints. TLS passthrough preserves cert validation and reduces mutual auth complexity.
- Keepalive & idle: set TCP idle timeout >= 120s and track connection reuse; our SDKs open pooled connections and reuse sockets aggressively.
- DNS resolution: if you rely on internal DNS filtering, ensure telemetry.redwood.com resolves to the allowed egress targets.
- Proxy support: we validate traffic initiated via an HTTP CONNECT proxy. Proxy must allow CONNECT to <telemetry.redwood.com>:443 and should preserve SNI.

Sample iptables SNAT rule (Linux NAT gateway):
  iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.10.0.0/16 -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source YOUR_EGRESS_IP

Fallbacks & fail-open behavior:
- If telemetry is blocked (e.g., during strict maintenance windows), inference traffic will continue but metrics/reporting will be delayed. We recommend a scheduled maintenance window rather than permanently dropping egress.
- For customers who cannot allow any outbound egress, we offer a locked-down on-prem runtime with periodic offline syncs; this requires additional ops and a packaging lead.

I'll prepare the CIDR snapshot once Naomi confirms the pilot endpoints list.

- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Can we schedule a 30 minute call tomorrow to walk the firewall team through the allowlist CSV and the VPC diagram? We're available 10–12 PST.
